description: Client Components are React components marked with the 'use client' directive. They run in the browser and are pre-rendered to HTML on the server during the initial page load. They can use React state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, and custom hooks. The 'use client' directive declares a boundary in the module graph: all imports and directly rendered components within that boundary are pulled into the client JavaScript bundle. Client Components should be treated as interactive leaf nodes in the component tree, not as wrappers for large subtrees.

constraints.title: 'use client' Boundary Pulls All Imports into the Client Bundle
constraints.problem: Once 'use client' is added to a file, every module imported by that file and every component it directly renders is included in the client JavaScript bundle, regardless of whether those dependencies need browser capabilities.
constraints.whyItMatters: A single misplaced 'use client' on a large component can inadvertently bundle server-only libraries, large data transformation utilities, or database clients into the client bundle. This inflates bundle size, increases parse time, degrades Core Web Vitals (LCP, TTI), and potentially leaks server-only code.
forbiddenPatterns: Adding 'use client' to layout.tsx or page.tsx when only a sub-component needs interactivity
Importing server-only utilities into a Client Component file
Placing 'use client' at the top of a barrel index file that re-exports many components
Wrapping large content trees in a single Client Component to add one interactive element
Importing heavy server-side libraries (ORM, fs, crypto) into a 'use client' file
allowedPatterns: Isolating 'use client' to the smallest interactive leaf component
Passing Server Components as children or props into Client Component wrappers
Using next/dynamic with ssr: false for non-critical client-only components
Importing only serializable data (strings, numbers, plain objects) from shared modules
productionRisks: Massive client JavaScript bundle inflating Time to Interactive (TTI)
Accidental inclusion of server-only code (database clients, secrets) in the browser bundle
Poor Lighthouse scores and Core Web Vitals degradation
Increased bandwidth costs for users on slow connections
architectureImplications: Client Components should be fine-grained islands of interactivity
The majority of a page's component tree should remain as Server Components
Large layouts should stay as Server Components with small Client Component islands embedded
optimizationGuidance: Push 'use client' as far down the tree as possible
Audit bundle with @next/bundle-analyzer after every new 'use client' boundary
Use next/dynamic for non-critical Client Components to enable lazy loading
quickFixes: Move 'use client' from the layout/page to the specific interactive child component
Extract just the interactive part (e.g., a search bar) into its own 'use client' file
architectureSuggestions: Think of Client Components as 'interactive islands': small, focused, and surrounded by server-rendered content
Pass all data needed by Client Components as serialized props from their Server Component parents

invalid:
'use client' // This pulls everything into the client bundle import Header from './header' import Footer from './footer' import DataTable from './data-table' import { db } from './db' // server-only! export default function Page() { return
}

constraints.title: Props Passed to Client Components Must Be Serializable
constraints.problem: Props passed from Server Components to Client Components must be serializable by React. Non-serializable values such as functions (other than Server Actions), class instances, Dates, Maps, Sets with complex values, and circular references cannot be passed as props.
constraints.whyItMatters: The boundary between Server and Client Components requires all data to be serialized into the RSC Payload (a binary wire format). Non-serializable values cannot traverse this boundary and will cause runtime errors or be silently dropped, leading to broken component state on the client.
forbiddenPatterns: Passing functions as props (other than Server Actions)
Passing class instances as props
Passing Symbol values as props
Passing BigInt values as props
Passing circular reference objects as props
Passing WeakMap, WeakSet, WeakRef as props
Passing Error objects as props
Passing database connection objects as props
Passing React elements created server-side as non-children props (complex patterns)
allowedPatterns: Plain objects and arrays of serializable values
Maps and Sets of serializable values
Server Actions (functions marked 'use server') passed as action props
JSX passed as children (rendered server-side and included in RSC Payload as rendered output)
productionRisks: Silent data loss when non-serializable props are dropped
Runtime crashes during RSC Payload parsing on the client
Hydration mismatches from inconsistent server/client data
Security vulnerabilities from accidentally serializing sensitive objects
architectureImplications: The Server-to-Client prop boundary enforces a DTO (Data Transfer Object) pattern naturally
All data transformation should happen server-side before serialization
Client Components should receive minimal, clean, flat data structures
optimizationGuidance: Always map database/API responses to plain DTOs before passing as props
Keep Client Component props interfaces simple and flat to reduce serialization overhead
quickFixes: Convert class instances to plain objects with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj))
Move function logic into a Server Action ('use server') if it must be passed as a prop
architectureSuggestions: Define explicit TypeScript interface DTOs for all Server-to-Client prop boundaries
Validate serializable shapes at compile time using TypeScript strict mode

invalid:
// Server Component passing a function prop
return <ClientComp onAction={() => db.update(id)} />

constraints.title: Server Components Must Not Be Imported into Client Component Module Graph
constraints.problem: Server Components (async components, components using server-only APIs) must not be directly imported by Client Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: When a Client Component imports another component, that import is pulled into the client bundle. If a Server Component is imported this way, Next.js cannot execute server-only code (database access, secret use) on the client and the component will fail. The correct pattern is to pass Server Components as children or props from a parent Server Component.
forbiddenPatterns: import ServerComponent from './server-component' inside a 'use client' file
Directly importing async Server Components into Client Components
Importing components that use next/headers, next/cookies, or 'server-only' into Client Components
allowedPatterns: Passing Server Components as named props: <ClientWrapper header={<ServerHeader />} />
Composing the combination from a parent Server Component that controls both
productionRisks: Server-only logic being executed on the client, causing authentication bypass or data exposure
Undefined behavior from async components in a synchronous client rendering context
architectureImplications: The interleaving of Server and Client Components must always be orchestrated from a Server Component parent
Client Components are opaque to their children's rendering environment; Server Components passed as children remain server-rendered
optimizationGuidance: Use the children/slot composition pattern to interleave server and client subtrees
Keep the component tree's outer layers as Server Components to maximize static rendering surface
quickFixes: Move the import to a parent Server Component and pass the result as children or a prop
Wrap the Server Component usage in the parent and thread it as a prop into the Client Component
architectureSuggestions: Establish a rule: Client Components never import Server Components. Composition flows top-down from Server Component parents.

constraints.title: Third-Party Components Without 'use client' Must Be Wrapped
constraints.problem: Third-party npm packages that use client-only React features (useState, useEffect, browser APIs) but do not include the 'use client' directive will fail when used directly in Server Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: Many third-party libraries were built before the React Server Components era and do not declare 'use client'. Next.js cannot automatically infer that these components require client-side execution. Using them in Server Components causes runtime errors.
forbiddenPatterns: Using third-party UI components (carousels, modals, date pickers, charts) that use hooks directly in Server Components without wrapping
Importing animation libraries (framer-motion, react-spring) without a 'use client' wrapper
Using form libraries (react-hook-form, formik) without a 'use client' wrapper
allowedPatterns: Creating a thin 'use client' wrapper file that re-exports the third-party component
Using the third-party component inside an existing 'use client' component
productionRisks: Runtime errors: 'useState is not defined' or similar
Developer confusion about which packages are compatible with Server Components
architectureImplications: Every third-party UI component must be audited for server compatibility
Create a central wrappers/ directory for Client Component wrappers around third-party libraries
optimizationGuidance: Create wrapper files early in the project for all major third-party UI dependencies
Document which wrappers are 'use client' in team conventions
quickFixes:
Create a new file: 'use client'
import { ThirdPartyComp } from 'third-party-lib'
export default ThirdPartyComp
architectureSuggestions: Maintain a components/wrappers/ directory containing 'use client' thin wrappers for all third-party components that need client-side execution

constraints.title: Avoid Calling Route Handlers from Client Components When Server Components Can Fetch Instead
constraints.problem: Client Components that fetch data by calling internal Next.js Route Handlers (/api routes) are adding an unnecessary network roundtrip that could be eliminated by fetching in a Server Component.
constraints.whyItMatters: A Client Component calling a Route Handler on the same Next.js server creates a server-to-server HTTP request (or at best a loopback). This doubles the latency compared to a Server Component directly calling the data source. It also prevents static prerendering of that data.
forbiddenPatterns: fetch('/api/data') inside a Client Component when the data could be fetched in a parent Server Component
useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/users') }, []) for initial data loading that could be server-fetched
Calling Route Handlers from Server Components (creates unnecessary network hop)
allowedPatterns: Server Components fetching data directly from databases or external APIs
Passing fetched data as serialized props to Client Components
Client Components using SWR or React Query only for client-side data that must be fresh (user interactions, polling)
productionRisks: Unnecessary network latency degrading Time to First Byte (TTFB)
Double data-fetching overhead on the server
architectureImplications: Initial data loading is a Server Component responsibility
Client Components trigger data mutations and handle real-time updates, not initial page data loads
optimizationGuidance: Audit all useEffect data-fetching patterns; migrate initial loads to Server Components
Reserve client-side fetching for truly dynamic data (user-triggered, real-time)
quickFixes: Move the fetch call to the parent Server Component and pass data as props to the Client Component
architectureSuggestions: Use a Server Component as a data-fetching shell that passes all needed data to Client Component children
Treat client-side data fetching (SWR, TanStack Query) as an optimization for updates, not initial load

valid:
// page.tsx (Server Component)
export default async function Page() { const users = await db.select().from(usersTable); return <UserList users={users} /> }
